title: Contextual Annotation Layer — prototype & usability audit
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design, prototype, and hand off a contextual annotation layer for the Console Insights and Rollouts surfaces. This layer allows engineers, PMs and reviewers to attach short annotations, reasoning and link to evals directly on timeline bands and heatmap tiles. Goal: reduce context switching when investigating cost/latency anomalies and make rollout rationale more discoverable.
summary: Create an accessible, low-visual-weight annotation UI that can be toggled on/off, supports inline comments, and surfaces linked artifacts (PR, eval dashboard). Deliver a clickable prototype, redlines for dev, and a short usability audit with remediation tasks.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype demonstrates: toggle on/off, create/edit/delete annotation, attach link, and resolved state
Visual spec includes spacing, colors, focus states, and compact variant for glance-mode
Accessibility audit completed with ARIA roles, keyboard flows, and color contrast fixes addressed
Dev handoff package (Figma redlines + tokens) uploaded and linked in ticket
PM sign-off on wording and visibility rules
qa_checklist: Annotations persist per-model and per-rollout timeline
Keyboard-only flows for create, edit, collapse, and dismiss work without mouse
Screen reader reads annotation header and attached link label
Toggle state respects user preference and persists across sessions
No layout shift > CLS threshold when annotations appear/disappear
comments: 2025-02-12 Aisha Patel: Initial ticket created. Attached early sketch and problem statement. Noted overlap with existing notes feature; objective is in-context attachments rather than long-form notes.

2025-02-13 Marco Nguyen: Quick feasibility check — backend will expose a flat annotations API (model/rollout/tile-level) but needs schema finalization. Flagging ENG-23456 as dependent for API contract.

2025-02-14 Leah Kim: PM feedback — prioritize compact collapsed state for glance mode; want a visual affordance for ‘has annotations’ without noise. Also require link to evals dashboard in the quick preview.

2025-02-15 Priya Shah: Accessibility pass — initial prototype fails color contrast on timestamp chip. Recommend swapping to token color palette token-accent-600 and add focus ring styles. Also request explicit aria-describedby for annotation body.
2025-02-16 Aisha Patel: Updated Figma with contrast fixes and keyboard flows. Added prototype microcopy suggestions for 'Resolve' vs 'Dismiss' language. Uploaded redlines export (see design_files).

2025-02-17 Ethan Ross: Engineering review notes — concern about render performance with 200+ annotations on a single heatmap. Trade-off options noted: virtualized render, server-side rollup, or a threshold that collapses older annotations (see decisions).

2025-02-18 Leah Kim: Stakeholder sync — approved visual weight and toggle placement. PM requests two follow-ups: analytics event spec (who views annotations) and a lightweight migration path for existing notes.
2025-02-18 Marco Nguyen: Marking as In Review and assigning dev ticket once ENG-23456 API schema is final.
decisions: Use a compact collapsed marker (dot + count) in glance/tile modes to minimize noise
Support two annotation types: 'Comment' (free text + links) and 'Audit' (structured tag + severity)
Backend API will provide basic pagination; client will virtualize rendering and lazily fetch details on expand
Avoid inline rich-text editing in v1 — plain text + URL attachment only to reduce parsing and XSS surface
tradeoffs: Performance vs discoverability: collapsed markers hide context but protect render performance on large result sets
Feature scope: delaying rich-text reduces implementation risk but may require a future migration for teams used to formatted notes
Storage: storing attachments as link references keeps annotation payload small but relies on external services for persistence
